title: JewelMind JDL v1 Canonical Document
description: Structural (schema-layer) validation for a JDL v1 Canonical Document. This schema mirrors the CURRENT backend Pydantic model (backend/jewelmind/domain/schema.py) exactly: it enforces types, literal/enum membership, and additionalProperties=false. It deliberately does NOT enforce jewelry business-rule thresholds (minimum band width, prong count set membership, positive dimensions, etc.) that the current backend enforces only at the semantic-validation layer (backend/jewelmind/validation/engine.py) rather than at the Pydantic/schema layer. See docs/bible/05-jdl/075-validation-pipeline.md for why these two layers are kept separate, and docs/bible/05-jdl/065-canonical-json-serialization.md for the one known schema-layer blind spot (non-finite numeric tokens).

bandTaper.description: MINOR, additive Sprint 17 field (see docs/bible/19-shank/README.md and docs/bible/05-jdl/081-schema-versioning-and-migrations.md). mode="NONE" (the default) is bit-identical to pre-Sprint-17 geometry; bottomRatio is ignored when mode="NONE".

bottomRatio.description: Fraction of the base (head) dimension retained at the bottom of the ring when mode="TOWARD_BOTTOM".

ArrangementGroup.description:
A named set of instances that move and are edited together.

Grouping is expressed by an instance naming its `groupId`, not by the group
listing members. One direction only: two directions would need to agree, and
a membership list that disagrees with its members is a malformed document
that nothing can resolve correctly.
ArrangementGroup.title: ArrangementGroup

ArrangementPattern.description:
A pattern plus what it applies to.

`sourceInstanceId` names the instance being repeated: a pattern is always
"more of this one", never a free-floating count of nothing. That keeps every
generated member's stone reference, gem and overrides traceable to a real
instance the user can see and edit.
ArrangementPattern.title: ArrangementPattern

ArrangementRelation.description:
A declared relationship between two or more instances or groups.

Relations are RECORDED AND VALIDATED, never solved. `resolve.py` checks that
every referenced ID exists and that the relation's arity is respected, and
passes them through untouched. Enforcing them — moving a stone because its
mirror moved — is a future editing capability, marked PLANNED rather than
implied.
ArrangementRelation.title: ArrangementRelation

GemIdentity.description:
What THIS stone actually is (brief sections 4/6/7/16).

This is what JDL stores per stone, and it is deliberately separate from the
registry entry it points at.

`gemId` alone is not an identity: a natural untreated sapphire and a
heat-treated lab-grown sapphire share a `gemId` and are different stones.
GemIdentity.title: GemIdentity

GemTreatment.description:
One treatment claim about one stone (brief section 7).

Treatments live on `GemIdentity`, never on a registry entry: whether a
particular ruby was heated is a fact about that stone.

JewelMind records the claim and its source. It does not decide whether a
treatment must be disclosed, whether it is stable, or whether it affects
durability — all of which require professional evidence
(GEM-GOV-006).
GemTreatment.title: GemTreatment

InstanceOverrides.description:
The EXPLICITLY supported per-instance deviations from the referenced
stone specification.

A CLOSED SET, on purpose. Allowing an instance to override any stone field
would make the reference meaningless — the instance would become a second
stone definition, and "same stone, eight times" would stop being expressible.
So an instance may scale a size and rotate itself, and nothing else. It can
never override the shape, the source, the outline, or the profile: those are
what make two occurrences occurrences OF something.

A field left `None` means "inherit", which is different from "same value as
the parent" — an inherited size follows a later edit to the stone
specification, a copied one would not.
InstanceOverrides.title: InstanceOverrides

InstancePlacement.description:
Where an instance sits, and how that was expressed.

`mode` records the ORIGIN of the placement so an editor can tell a position
the user typed from one a pattern produced. Resolution rewrites every mode
to `EXPLICIT`; before that, a `PATTERN_MEMBER` placement's transform is the
pattern's own offset for that member and is not yet the final position.
InstancePlacement.title: InstancePlacement

InstanceTransform.description:
An instance's rigid placement: a translation plus one rotation.

ONE ROTATION, ABOUT THE VERTICAL AXIS ONLY, and that is a decision rather
than an omission. `StoneSpec.orientation` already rotates a stone about its
own vertical axis, and a full 3×3 orientation here would create a second,
overlapping way to express the same thing plus five more ways to express
something no current geometry builder can execute. Tilt and roll are
recorded as PLANNED in the capability registry instead of being accepted
and ignored.

Millimetres and degrees, like every other length and angle in JewelMind
(LAW-007). No unit field, no conversion.
InstanceTransform.title: InstanceTransform

LinearPatternSpec.description:
`count` copies along a straight line, evenly spaced.

`spacingMm` is centre-to-centre distance. It is a POSITION parameter, never
a clearance: nothing here knows a stone's size, so nothing here can claim
two stones do not collide. Whether a spacing is manufacturable is a
geometric and professional question, asked downstream.
LinearPatternSpec.title: LinearPatternSpec

MirrorPatternSpec.description:
One reflected copy across a principal plane through the design origin.

A pattern rather than a relation because it PRODUCES an instance. The
`MIRRORED_PAIR` relation records that two existing instances are a pair;
this creates the second one.
MirrorPatternSpec.title: MirrorPatternSpec

RadialPatternSpec.description:
`count` copies around a circle of radius `radiusMm`.

`startAngleDeg` and `sweepDeg` make a partial arc expressible, so a halo
that stops short of the shank is a first-class arrangement rather than a
full circle with members deleted.
RadialPatternSpec.title: RadialPatternSpec

StoneInstanceDef.description:
One occurrence of a stone in a design.

References the stone specification and the gem identity rather than
restating them (see this module's docstring). `stoneRef` is a symbolic name
resolved by the consumer — `"primary"` means the definition's own
`stone` — which is what keeps this model free of a `StoneSpec` import and
therefore free of the whole domain schema.

Supersedes `jewelmind.gem.models.StoneInstance`, which carried identity and
role but deliberately no placement (it predates this layer). That model
remains for gem-only consumers; this one is what an arrangement holds.
StoneInstanceDef.title: StoneInstanceDef

arrangement.description: Stone Arrangement Engine v1 (Sprint 22). OPTIONAL and nullable: a document without it is a single-stone design and behaves exactly as before, which is why adding this field is a MINOR, additive change and schemaVersion stays "0.1.0". Instance/group/pattern/relation ids are the authoritative identity; array order carries no meaning and is canonicalized before hashing. Structural validity is enforced here; whether the arrangement RESOLVES is the semantic layer's job (JM-ARRANGE-001..006), per 075-validation-pipeline.md's layering. Multi-stone GEOMETRY generation is PARTIAL — see docs/bible/24-arrangement/execution-boundary.md.
arrangement.title: ArrangementDefinition

JdlCustomOutline.description:
A caller-supplied closed stone outline (brief section 23).

Ordered points only. No JDL representation may ever carry an expression,
script or function body (JDL's no-executable-code rule), and a point list
is the representation that cannot.

The outline is closed implicitly; the first point must not be repeated at
the end. Semantic validation (self-intersection, zero area, degenerate
segments) lives in `jewelmind/stone/outline_validation.py`, not here —
structural and semantic validation stay separate layers.
JdlCustomOutline.title: JdlCustomOutline

JdlGemIdentity.description:
What gem THIS stone is (brief sections 3/4/17).

Deliberately separate from every geometry field. A round stone is not
automatically a diamond, and the same `StoneSpec` is reusable with any gem —
which is why this is its own object rather than a `stone.material` string.

`gemId` references the canonical registry
(`backend/jewelmind/gem/registry.py`). IDs are language-independent and
constrained so one can never become a filesystem path or a shell argument.

Absent entirely on a legacy document, which normalizes to `unknown` — never
to diamond (brief section 18).
JdlGemIdentity.title: JdlGemIdentity

JdlGemTreatment.description:
One treatment claim about this stone (brief section 7).

JewelMind records the claim and who made it. It never decides whether a
treatment must be disclosed, whether it is stable, or whether it affects
durability — all of which need professional evidence this project does not
have.
JdlGemTreatment.title: JdlGemTreatment

JdlImportedStoneAsset.description:
Reference to externally supplied stone geometry (brief sections 30/31).

`assetHash` is a content hash, never a filesystem path: a path in a design
document would leak an internal server location into every export and
review package (FOUNDRY-GOV-011).

`declaredUnit` is required rather than inferred, because no format
JewelMind reads carries a reliable, universally-populated unit, and
guessing one silently rescales a real physical object.
JdlImportedStoneAsset.title: JdlImportedStoneAsset

JdlOutlinePoint.description: One 2D point of a custom stone outline, in the stone's local frame.
JdlOutlinePoint.title: JdlOutlinePoint

JdlStoneMeasurement.description:
Provenance for a physically measured stone (brief section 28).

Every field is optional and caller-supplied. JewelMind never fills one in:
an absent measurement source is an honest absence, not a value to invent
(STONEV2-GOV-006).
JdlStoneMeasurement.title: JdlStoneMeasurement

schemaVersion.description: The only JDL schema version currently accepted. Default when omitted: "0.1.0".

size.description: EU/French ring size. Positivity and range (1 < size < 50) are semantic rule JM-RING-002, not enforced here.

innerDiameter.description: Millimeters. Range (10 < x < 30) is semantic rule JM-RING-001, not enforced here.

width.description: Millimeters. Minimum 1.5mm / maximum-warning 12mm are semantic rules JM-BAND-001/JM-BAND-003, not enforced here.

thickness.description: Millimeters. Minimum 1.4mm is semantic rule JM-BAND-002, not enforced here.

stone.description: MINOR, additive Sprint 18 field set (see docs/bible/20-stone/README.md and docs/bible/05-jdl/081-schema-versioning-and-migrations.md): shape gained 6 new enum members, length/width/orientation are new optional fields. `diameter` required (only meaningfully) for shape="round"; `length`/`width` required (only meaningfully) for every other shape — enforced at the semantic/Pydantic layer (StoneSpec's own model_validator), deliberately not as a JSON-Schema if/then conditional here, per 075-validation-pipeline.md's structural/semantic layering. Sprint 22 note: the properties added by Sprints 19-21 (bezel wall dimensions; stone source/profile/narrowWidth/customOutline/measurement/importedAsset; gem identity) were missing from this schema and are now present, generated from the live Pydantic models. Until then this schema structurally rejected documents the backend accepts.

diameter.description: Millimeters. Meaningful only when shape="round". Range (2mm to 15mm) is semantic rule JM-STONE-001, not enforced here.

length.description: Millimeters. Major horizontal dimension (local Y axis). Required (semantic layer) when shape != "round".

width.description: Millimeters. Minor horizontal dimension (local X axis). Required (semantic layer) when shape != "round".

depth.description: Millimeters. Range is semantic rule JM-STONE-002, not enforced here.

orientation.description: Degrees, rotation around the stone's local vertical axis. See docs/bible/20-stone/565-stone-coordinate-and-orientation.md.

prongCount.description: Deliberately NOT constrained to {4, 6} at this layer. The current backend intentionally keeps prong-count set membership as semantic rule JM-PRONG-001 so an out-of-set value produces a structured diagnostic rather than a raw schema-parse error (see backend/jewelmind/domain/schema.py comment on SettingSpec.prongCount).

prongDiameter.description: Millimeters. Minimum 0.8mm is semantic rule JM-PRONG-002, not enforced here.

prongHeight.description: Millimeters. Must exceed basketHeight per semantic rule JM-PRONG-004, not enforced here.

basketHeight.description: Millimeters. Positivity and 8mm warning ceiling are semantic rules JM-SETTING-001/JM-SETTING-002, not enforced here.

setting.description: Sprint 22 note: the properties added by Sprints 19-21 (bezel wall dimensions; stone source/profile/narrowWidth/customOutline/measurement/importedAsset; gem identity) were missing from this schema and are now present, generated from the live Pydantic models. Until then this schema structurally rejected documents the backend accepts. Sprint 23 note: prongStyle, headArchitecture, seatMode, prongTipRatio, headBaseRatio, pegDiameter and pegHeight are additive optional fields, each defaulting to the pre-Sprint-23 behaviour (ROUND_PRONG / BASKET / NONE), so every existing document generates byte-identical geometry and schemaVersion stays 0.1.0.

meshTolerance.description: Millimeters. Positivity IS enforced structurally here, matching Pydantic Field(gt=0) on PreviewSpec.meshTolerance.

angularTolerance.description: Radians (confirmed by inspecting the installed CadQuery source: Shape.mesh() passes this value directly into OCCT's BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh angular-deflection parameter, which OCCT documents in radians). Positivity IS enforced structurally here, matching Pydantic Field(gt=0).
